newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Chinatrust Bank to merge with U.S. ally.
newsitem.headline: Chinatrust Bank to merge with U.S. ally.

text.p: Chinatrust Commercial Bank, one of Taiwan's leading private banks, said on Monday it planned to merge with U.S.-based Chinatrust Bank of California and Chinatrust Bank of New York.
A company spokeswoman quoted Chinatrust chairman Jeffrey Koo as announcing the merger with the two U.S. banks, which have combined assets of US$1 billion.
Koo said Chinatrust, aiming to become one of the world's top 100 banks by 2000, was also evaluating the feasibility of setting up a branch in Russia.
The two U.S. banks, which were invested personally by Koo and Chinatrust president Kenneth Lo, had already merged into one bank in April in preparation for the final merger with Taiwan's Chinatrust.

Chinatrust had total assets of T$456.8 billion as of end June, which means the group's total asset after the merger would be close to T$500 billion. Chinatrust currently has 13 overseas branches, representative offices and joint-venture banks in Hong Kong, Tokyo, India, Vietnam, London and Paraguay.
